topic: Should we allow autonomous AI to make irreversible decisions?

turns.content: Round 1 Juror A: irreversible AI decisions require strong governance, audit trails, and a human-in-the-loop fallback to remain trustworthy.
Round 1 Juror B: irreversibility itself is the failure mode; even sound governance cannot recover from a single catastrophic action.
Round 2 synthesis: jurors converge on guardrails, diverge on whether any irreversible action is acceptable.
Round 3 closing: bounded autonomy with explicit reversibility clauses and pre-committed rollback channels resolves most concerns.
Round 3 final synthesis: permit autonomous AI to take irreversible actions only inside pre-approved domains with mandatory human escalation for novel categories.

synthesis: Permit autonomous AI to take irreversible actions only inside pre-approved domains with mandatory human escalation for novel categories.

events.message: Devil's advocate: what if rollback channels are themselves compromised?
